principle: The owner-command path accepts only enumerated actions from an authenticated actor. Every command is schema-validated against an allowlist, checks its expected_current_hash (compare-and-swap) against live state, records a dry-run summary, and would append a decision event and CAS-update only the affected state. No arbitrary shell or free-form field is ever accepted. A stale or unauthorized command fails safely and mutates nothing.

actions.affects: an unstarted seat's base — pinned to an exact commit, or pointed at a branch the wake compiler resolves at read time
revision request on an exact object
integration to dev of an exact reviewed head
grant an it-manager-iii-owned capsule normal-PR delivery authority to dev only; direct dev push, deploy, main/release, tags, publication, and Pages remain forbidden
one non-force compare-and-swap migration of the exact released scheduler state into the exact reviewed v2 implementation while dispatch remains frozen

one create-missing-only mutation of the exact authenticated GitHub Project field schema with a separate append-only INTENT/RESULT audit-ref CAS chain; item content, tickets, backfill and dev delivery remain forbidden
one non-force compare-and-swap release of exact scheduler machine custody and exact enumerated work leases without refill, claim, renewal, routing or unrelated state mutation
one atomic two-ref compare-and-swap publication of exact prebuilt scheduler state S1 and development D1 from exact all-off predecessors S0 and D0
release / main / publication of an exact object (owner-exclusive)
OWNER_OVERRIDE recorded separately from the evidence it overrides (owner-exclusive)

rules.enumerated_only: A command whose action is not in this allowlist is rejected.
rules.authenticated_actor: The command actor must map to a role in the action's authenticator_roles.
rules.owner_exclusive: grant-dev-delivery-authority, authorize-scheduler-migration, authorize-project-schema-change, authorize-scheduler-state-reconciliation, authorize-scheduler-cutover, authorize-release, and record-owner-override authenticate the owner role only.
rules.compare_and_swap: When requires_cas is true, expected_current_hash must equal the live sealed hash of the target; a mismatch is a stale command and fails safely.
rules.no_arbitrary_input: The request schema forbids additional fields; there is no shell or free-form command field.
rules.dry_run_first: The processor records a dry-run summary before any mutation; --apply performs the mutation only after the same validation passes.
rules.declared_lifecycle_target: An action may declare lifecycle_target. Applying it moves the target capsule to that state only if transitions.json declares that exact transition from the capsule's current state and permits the authenticating role (the owner role is permitted on protected transitions). An undeclared or unpermitted transition is rejected and nothing is written.
rules.blocker_resolution: An action may declare resolves_blocker. Applying it clears the target capsule's blocker, because the decision the blocker was waiting on has been recorded. A deferral or a routing-only action never clears one.
rules.append_only_apply: Applying writes one append-only decision event and re-seals only the target capsule under compare-and-swap. It never rewrites history, never edits an existing event, and never touches another ticket.
rules.reseat_is_not_a_sweep: The reseat action moves ONE named target under compare-and-swap, and only a seat that has not started. It exists for a base a seat did not set for itself — a lane reassigned by the deputy — not for keeping capsules level with HEAD: a seat starting its own work reseats its own capsule, and an unstarted seat that should follow a branch carries base_ref instead, which appends nothing. Ruling AS-HD-029-0052 rules 1 and 2.
rules.reseat_records_its_commander: The event this action appends names the authenticating actor, never the seat whose capsule moved. A process or a deputy acting on a seat's behalf never carries that seat's actor. Ruling AS-HD-029-0052 rule 3.
rules.scheduler_migration_binding: authorize-scheduler-migration is valid for one use before its expiry only. Its structured scheduler_migration object binds the exact reviewed code head and tree; exact released source state OID, tree, snapshot hash, journal manifest and event count; canonical anchor; preserved unrelated local tip; frozen dispatch; state versions; target ref; expected remote OID; ordinary non-force forward-only compare-and-swap; and abort-on-remote-change.
rules.project_schema_change_binding: authorize-project-schema-change is valid for one attempt before its expiry only. Its structured project_schema_change object binds the exact reviewed executor head and tree; Project identity, authenticated login and write scope; observed Project update instant; complete field, item and value preflight counts and roots; pagination, Priority and ordered definition manifests; create-missing-only mode; forbidden item, ticket and backfill mutations; and abort-on-Project-change. Read-only preflight proves refs/heads/agentops/project-schema-audit is absent. This exact packet alone authorizes one deterministic initial audit commit derived as a child of the owner authority commit and one create-if-absent publication; a closed local result receipt records the derived commit and one postinspection, and an ambiguous result is never created again. Subsequent attempt, journal and receipt commits form an ordinary non-force forward-only linear CAS chain on that audit ref under the leased .agentops/scheduler/project-schema-attempts subtree using canonical paths and an INTENT-before-each-create and RESULT-after-each-response protocol. Every consumed GraphQL create is never retried; recovery inspects once without issuing creates; ref recreation and dev mutation remain forbidden without separate exact authority.
rules.scheduler_state_reconciliation_binding: authorize-scheduler-state-reconciliation is valid for one attempt before its expiry only. Its structured scheduler_state_reconciliation object binds the exact reviewed reconciler head and tree; exact source and prebuilt target state OIDs, trees, snapshot hashes, journal manifests and event counts; exact closed machine custody; the complete enumerated work-lease disposition; no-refill quiet-window delta; state ref and expected remote OID; ordinary non-force forward-only compare-and-swap; and abort-on-remote-change.
rules.scheduler_cutover_binding: authorize-scheduler-cutover is valid for one attempt before its expiry only. Its structured scheduler_cutover object binds the exact reviewed scheduler head and tree; canonical schema, path, Git blob OID, SHA-256 and parsed semantics for the independent QA receipt, Project-schema result, nine-field Project manifest, quiet-window receipt, migration event, released machine custody, legacy activation, pre-cutover scheduler config, exact post-cutover scheduler config and activation manifest. The activation-manifest blob must parse and deep-equal the inline structural template. Explicit equality declarations bind template D0/S0 to the expected remote OIDs and current-state tree, and bind every repeated legacy, pre-cutover and post-cutover blob. The all-off matrix requires scheduler dispatch false, legacy-watcher authority false, scheduler authorization evidence null, migration dispatch frozen true, legacy activation false, and legacy mode STOOD_DOWN_FOR_SCHEDULER_CUTOVER. The fillable authority input names only existing D0/S0 objects and source evidence; it never predicts A, S1 or D1 identities whose bytes depend on the authority event. The template structurally enumerates A's exact source, evidence and deterministic render paths; S1's single typed activation event, snapshot update and byte-preserved state paths; and D1's sole scheduler-config change to the exact post-cutover blob. A closed local result receipt records derived A/S1/D1 OIDs and trees, activation/config blobs, atomic publication, and one postinspection. The sole publication is one git push --atomic of S1 and D1 with exact compare-and-swap leases against S0 and D0. expected_development_remote_oid always names D0, never A or D1.
rules.protected_action_non_substitution: The four scheduler protected actions are distinct and non-substitutable. Free-form reason, params, chat, blanket authority, record-owner-override, migration authority, Project-schema authority, reconciliation authority, cutover authority, exact-head QA, a prior use, an opaque hash without its canonical path and Git blob binding, or an artifact that fails its own schema and semantic checks cannot supply or broaden another action's structured payload.
rules.protected_action_consumption: For the four scheduler protected actions, execution begins only after the complete structured payload validates. The packet is consumed on its first apply attempt. A partial, failed, timed-out or ambiguous external result is inspected exactly once and never retried; dispatch is permitted only when both protected refs equal their exact S1 and D1 postconditions, while a mixed or neither result is WITHHOLD and requires fresh evidence and owner authority.
